analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow excerpts, patches, documentation and file metadata against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. No concrete regression is established. In ci.yml:665–699 and the corresponding cluster jobs, new .git caches use pinned actions, discard structurally invalid repositories, disable checkout credential persistence, and condition saves on SAVE_CACHES. fsck checks connectivity, not cache provenance; the evidence does not establish an adversarial writer to these cache entries. Cluster build caching at 915–970 retains toolchain/pin/path binding and content-checked timestamp restoration through an external helper. Coverage uploads at 643–653 contain reports, not observed runtime secrets. The nonblocking GPU lane and Provider Tests gate at 1107–1202 are unchanged according to the complete range map, so their exclusions are not new findings.
component-changes.yml:12–13,28 exports a new mimo_audio selector without changing permissions. docs-impact.yml:61–68 introduces partial/sparse checkout while retaining commit-signature checks, full commit history and the existing validation steps. There is no demonstrated policy bypass from excluding compressed evidence and landing media.
Security-relevant integration contracts remain: verify the changed classifier and MiMo gate consumers include every required input; verify SAVE_CACHES enforcement in the composite build action and routing changes; verify build-cache keys and timestamp restoration cannot reuse incompatible products; reconcile the documented CMake image provenance with the changed installer implementation (build.md patch, head 170–174). Also confirm sparse exclusions do not omit files actually required by changed validation paths. These implementations are outside this batch, not observed missing controls. Relevant assets/boundaries are A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054 for artifact integrity, TB-007/T-041/T-050 for numerical/cache/media gates, and A-018 for availability. No supplied change directly alters serving authorization, hop encryption, prompt storage, billing, or privileged helper controls.
